rows.selection_reason: Existing evidence is sparse, so this experiment tests a baseline multimodal configuration (singleprofile, PCA + ResNet50, concat fusion) to evaluate if combining RNA and image data improves accuracy. It isolates the effect of multimodal fusion and provides foundational insights to guide subsequent choices.

The existing evidence shows config_016 (multimodal, singleprofile, concat fusion) achieves 0.5266 validation accuracy. This experiment tests whether changing fusion from concat to weighted (config_017) improves performance, isolating the effect of fusion strategy. It's a logical extension of the previous configuration, testing a key design choice with minimal parameter changes, while balancing exploitation of the multimodal direction and exploration of fusion methods.

Existing evidence shows multimodal singleprofile models with concat fusion (config_016: 0.526 accuracy) outperform weighted fusion. This experiment tests whether using aggregation (avgpool) in a multimodal multiprofile setup improves performance, isolating the impact of profile setting and aggregation. It extends the current best configuration by exploring multiprofile (a key design choice) while maintaining consistent RNA/image encoders and fusion method, balancing exploration and exploitation.

The existing evidence shows that config_018 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, avgpool, concat) achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.6186). This experiment tests changing the aggregation method from avgpool to transformer while keeping other parameters the same, isolating the effect of aggregation. This balances exploitation of the current best configuration with exploration of a potentially impactful design choice.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal multiprofile models with avgpool aggregation and concat fusion (e.g., config_018) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.6186). This experiment tests replacing the RNA encoder from pca_n2000 to scvi_n200 in this high-performing setup to determine if the RNA representation significantly impacts performance. This clarifies the importance of RNA encoder choice while keeping other components (image encoder, aggregation, fusion) consistent, balancing exploitation of the current best configuration with exploration of key design choices.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile settings and scvi_n200 RNA encoder (e.g., config_030) achieve high validation accuracy (0.6315). This experiment tests whether switching from concat to weighted fusion (config_031) further improves performance, isolating the effect of fusion method. It is a logical extension of the top-performing configuration and balances exploitation of promising directions with exploration of critical design choices.

The existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 RNA encoder, resnet50 image encoder, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_031) achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.6776). This experiment tests whether switching aggregation from avgpool to transformer (while keeping scvi_n200, resnet50, and weighted fusion) could further improve performance. It isolates the effect of aggregation method, a critical design choice, and builds on the strong foundation of the current top-performing configuration.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile settings, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion (e.g., config_033) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.713). This experiment tests scgpt RNA encoder with imagenet_vit_l image encoder, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion, which could further improve performance by combining a more advanced RNA encoder (scgpt) with the proven effective image encoder (imagenet_vit_l) and fusion strategy. This isolates the impact of RNA encoder choice while maintaining the high-performing components from the current best model.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion (e.g., config_033) achieve high accuracy (0.713). This experiment tests replacing the image encoder with imagenet_vit_l (a stronger vision transformer) while keeping other components identical. It directly isolates the impact of the image encoder on performance, addressing uncertainty about whether ViT outperforms ResNet50. This is the best use of the final experiment to potentially break the current accuracy record.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile settings and transformer aggregation achieve high accuracy (e.g., config_039: 0.725). This experiment tests whether using concat fusion instead of weighted fusion (as in config_039) could improve performance, isolating the effect of fusion type. It is the best use of the final experiment to validate if the current best's fusion method is optimal.
